_note: The transcendent function: the name and the mathematical analogy (CW6 ¶184, ¶828, CW8 ¶131, CW7 ¶121), the transition it makes possible (CW8 ¶145, CW11 ¶780), the living third (CW8 ¶189, CW7 ¶360, the tortoise seminar) and the method (CW14 ¶257, CW18 ¶1554). Van Eenwyk carries the section where the concept names a dynamical system. Quotations are placed by the corpus; nothing is typed.
line: The function that arises between the opposites: not a compromise but a living third, produced from the tension and making the transition to a new attitude organically possible.

sections.title: The name
sections.line: The word is borrowed from mathematics — a function of real and imaginary quantities — and used with the analogy held openly.

quotes.quote: This function of mediation between the opposites I have termed the transcendent function, by which I mean nothing mysterious, but merely a combined function of conscious and unconscious elements, or, as in mathematics, a common function of real and imaginary quantities.

There is nothing mysterious or metaphysical about the term "transcendent function." It means a psychological function comparable in its way to a mathematical function of the same name, which is a function of real and imaginary numbers.

“function” being here understood not as a basic function but as a complex function made up of other functions, and “transcendent” not as denoting a metaphysical quality but merely the fact that this function facilitates a transition from one attitude to another.

It has been named the “transcendent function”1 because it represents a function based on real and “imaginary,” or rational and irrational, data, thus bridging the yawning gulf between conscious and unconscious.

sections.title: The transition
sections.line: It is called transcendent because it carries a person from one attitude to another without discarding the unconscious — a process and a method at once.

quotes.quote: It is called "transcendent" because it makes the transition from one attitude to another organically possible, without loss of the unconscious.
The whole process is called the “transcendent function.” It is a process and a method at the same time.

sections.title: The living third
sections.line: The function is what happens when the confrontation is held: the tension produces a third thing that neither side contained.

quotes.quote: The confrontation of the two positions generates a tension charged with energy and creates a living, third thing

The secret of alchemy was in fact the transcendent function, the transformation of personality through the blending and fusion of the noble with the base components, of the differentiated with the inferior functions, of the conscious with the unconscious.
The characteristics of the tortoise are the characteristics of the transcendent function, the one that unites the pairs of opposites

sections.title: The method
sections.line: In practice the function is a method as much as an event: the conscious realisation of what the unconscious has produced.

quotes.quote: This continual process of getting to know the counterposition in the unconscious I have called the “transcendent function,”472 because the confrontation of conscious (rational) data with those that are unconscious (irrational) necessarily results in a modification of standpoint.
The cooperation of conscious reasoning with the data of the unconscious is called the “transcendent function”

sections.title: The third as a system
sections.line: Read as a dynamical system, the function describes order emerging from tension — a result no side of the opposition could have produced alone.

quotes.quote: whereby chaotic dynamics actually generate a higher order result coming out than existed going in
